EXACT PUBLISH SEQUENCE TO RUN ONCE NPM AUTH IS LIVE (order doesn't matter since no cross-dependency, but doing runtime-web first is tidy):

cd /Users/pablofernandez/Work/nostr-multi-platform/.wt-npm-prep/web/packages/runtime-web
CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang \
AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar \
npm publish --tag rc --access public

cd /Users/pablofernandez/Work/nostr-multi-platform/.wt-npm-prep/web/packages/components-web
npm publish --tag rc --access public

`--tag rc` is required for both: npm's default dist-tag is always `latest` regardless of the version string being a prerelease (npm does NOT auto-detect prerelease semver and skip `latest`), so omitting it would make `latest` point at 1.0.0-rc.1 on the very first publish. `--access public` is redundant since both package.json already set `publishConfig.access: "public"`, but it's a harmless explicit safety net for scoped packages.  [...] CORRECTION TO YOUR ASSUMPTION: components-web does NOT depend on runtime-web. I grepped both packages' source and package.json — no reference either direction. They're independent sibling packages; each generates/vendors its own FlatBuffers wire bindings under src/generated/nmp/, and both merely happen to share the `flatbuffers` npm dependency. Only the in-repo, unpublished nmp-gallery and registry apps import both together. So there's no build-order requirement and no cross-package dependency to declare for consumers — each publishes fully independently.
 [...] REAL BLOCKER FOUND (not CI-specific — reproduces locally on this Mac too, contradicting the old assumption that secp256k1-sys/wasm32 issues were CI-only): runtime-web's `build:wasm` step compiles the `nmp-browser-runtime` Rust crate to wasm32-unknown-unknown via wasm-pack, which transitively builds `secp256k1-sys` (C code) for that target. Apple's Xcode-bundled clang (21.0.0) has no WebAssembly backend registered, so it fails with "unable to create target: 'No available targets are compatible with triple wasm32-unknown-unknown'". Homebrew's LLVM clang (`/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang`, already installed on this machine) DOES support wasm32/wasm64. Fix: point cc-rs at it via env vars:

CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang
AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar

With those set, `npm run build` in runtime-web completes cleanly (~45-90s: cargo release build + wasm-pack + wasm-opt). [...] 
CRITICAL GOTCHA FOR YOUR PUBLISH STEP: both `npm pack` and `npm publish` trigger the `prepack` script, which for runtime-web is `npm run build` — i.e. the FULL wasm rebuild reruns on every pack/publish invocation, not just on my manual build. You MUST set those two env vars on the `npm publish` command itself (not just have built once before), or publish will fail at the prepack step.
 [...] npm install: RESOLVES cleanly against the public registry. Note the scope mismatch you flagged was real — renamed @nmp/runtime-web -> @nmpis/runtime-web and @nmp/components-web -> @nmpis/components-web (^1.0.0-rc.1) in apps/web/package.json, dropped the dead tsconfig.json `paths` mapping to nonexistent ../packages/*, and moved several deep `@nmp/components-web/src/user-avatar/{ProfileWire,NostrProfileHost,NostrAvatar}` reach-through imports onto the package's actual public `./user-avatar` subpath export (confirmed via npm pack that all three re-export from there).
